hoursConvention: hours[0] is Sunday through hours[6] is Saturday, matching JavaScript getDay(). null means closed that day. A close time earlier than the open time means it closes after midnight.
priceNote: priceUSD is a typical counter price, not a quote. Prices move. The scoring form asks what you actually paid and uses that for the value index.

clusters.label: Hampden
clusters.blurb: Two scratch bakeries 225 metres apart on Chestnut Avenue.

clusters.label: Remington & Charles Village
clusters.blurb: The Howard Street corridor, plus the only stop open past midnight.

clusters.label: Mount Vernon & downtown
clusters.blurb: Antique Row and the old downtown pastry houses.

clusters.label: Little Italy & Harbor East
clusters.blurb: Two serious bakeries three hundred metres apart.

clusters.label: Fells Point
clusters.blurb: Waterfront, and the best place on the list to sit down.

clusters.label: Canton & Highlandtown
clusters.blurb: O'Donnell Square and the longest bakery hours here.

clusters.label: Federal Hill
clusters.blurb: South of the harbour, afternoons only.

stops.name: Ovenbird Bakery
stops.blurb: A sourdough bakery whose cookie became the reason people queue. Belgian milk chocolate is shaved into the dough rather than dropped in as chips, then finished with Maldon salt. You get chocolate in thin sheets through the crumb instead of molten pockets, which is a real technique difference worth scoring.

menu.name: Chocolate ChiRp Cookie
menu.note: Shaved Belgian milk chocolate, Maldon salt.

menu.name: Morning bun
menu.note: Laminated, cinnamon sugar. Gone by mid morning.

menu.name: Country sourdough loaf
menu.note: What the bakery is actually built on.

stops.name: Harmony Bakery
stops.blurb: Entirely vegan, gluten free and soy free, with flours blended in house. Whether that helps or hurts a chocolate chip cookie is exactly the question a rubric should be able to settle, which makes Harmony the control case for anyone who thinks they already know the answer.

menu.name: Chocolate chip cookie
menu.note: Vegan, gluten free, soy free.

menu.name: Spinach pie
menu.note: Savoury reset between sweet stops.

menu.name: Pizza slice
menu.note: Makes this a real stop, not a counter visit.

stops.name: Common Ground
stops.blurb: A worker cooperative cafe that bakes its own cookies, scones and muffins from scratch every morning. Less precious than the pastry shops on this list and cheaper than all of them, which makes it a useful test of whether technique or freshness is doing the work. Closed Wednesdays, which catches people out.

menu.name: Chocolate chip cookie
menu.note: Baked in house each morning.

menu.name: Muffin
menu.note: The other thing they are known for.

menu.name: Drip coffee
menu.note: Cheapest palate reset in Hampden.

stops.name: La Maison by Café Dear Leon
stops.blurb: The Remington sibling of the Canton cafe, and by far the biggest room on this list: 5,000 square feet, 155 seats inside and another 68 on the patio. A Korean American take on a French boulangerie. Better known for its s'mores cookie than its plain chocolate chip, so treat the chocolate chip as a good bet rather than a promise.

menu.name: Chocolate chip cookie
menu.note: Rotates with the daily pastry case.

menu.name: S'mores cookie
menu.note: The one that shows up in every photo.

menu.name: Latte
menu.note: Palate reset, and there is space to sit.

stops.name: Insomnia Cookies
stops.blurb: A chain, included on purpose. It is open until 3am near Hopkins, it sells a warm chocolate chip cookie for about two dollars, and it is the baseline every independent bakery here is quietly competing against. If a five dollar artisan cookie cannot beat it on your own rubric, that result is worth knowing.

menu.name: Classic chocolate chip
menu.note: Served warm. The control sample.

menu.name: Chocolate chunk deluxe
menu.note: Thicker, more chocolate, higher price.

menu.name: Double chocolate chunk
menu.note: For the chocolate factor comparison.

stops.name: Aunt Kelly's Cookies
stops.blurb: A cookie shop, not a bakery that happens to sell cookies, which makes it the closest thing this list has to a benchmark. Black owned, on Mount Vernon's Antique Row, baking daily. Butter crunch is the famous one. Chocolate chip is the one people argue about. Closes at 5 and shuts Sunday and Monday, so it shapes your route more than anything else here.

menu.name: Chocolate chip cookie
menu.note: Baked daily on site.

menu.name: Butter crunch
menu.note: The one that made the shop's name.

menu.name: Butter pecan
menu.note: Third in the rotation of favourites.

stops.name: Patisserie Poupon
stops.blurb: A genuinely French patisserie that has been downtown for decades. Cookies are on the menu, but the house is built on canelés, croissants and tiramisu. Include it if you want to test whether classical French technique produces a better American cookie. Sometimes the answer is no, and that is still a finding.

menu.name: Chocolate chip cookie
menu.note: On the cookie case some days.

menu.name: Canelé
menu.note: What the place is actually famous for.

menu.name: Pain au chocolat
menu.note: A second read on their chocolate sourcing.

stops.name: Ovenbird Bakery
stops.blurb: The original Ovenbird, and the most useful control in the whole tour. Same recipe as the Rotunda shop, different oven, different baker on shift. If your scores diverge between the two, that tells you something about your own palate before it tells you anything about the cookie.

menu.name: Chocolate ChiRp Cookie
menu.note: Shaved Belgian milk chocolate, Maldon salt.

menu.name: Focaccia
menu.note: The Little Italy shop leans savoury.

menu.name: Country sourdough loaf
menu.note: The bakery's foundation.

stops.name: Kneads Bakeshop
stops.blurb: An artisan bakeshop and cafe doing handcrafted breads and a proper cafe menu, open seven days from 7 to 5. That makes it the most reliable stop here: no rotating list, no early close, chocolate chip on the counter every day. Three hundred metres from Ovenbird's Little Italy shop, so the two make an easy back to back comparison.

menu.name: Chocolate chip chunk cookie
menu.note: On the counter every day.

menu.name: Sprinkledoodle
menu.note: House twist on a snickerdoodle.

menu.name: Oatmeal raisin
menu.note: The control for people who claim to prefer it.

stops.name: Pitango Bakery + Café
stops.blurb: On a quiet waterfront side street, and open until 9 or 10 at night, which no other bakery here manages. That makes it the one stop that works as an actual sit down date rather than a counter visit. Italian leaning. Chocolate chip cookies appear some days and not others.

menu.name: Chocolate chip cookie
menu.note: Appears on the case some days.

menu.name: Cornetto
menu.note: The Italian answer to a croissant.

menu.name: Espresso
menu.note: Sit down and reset.

stops.name: Sacré Sucré
stops.blurb: Macarons are the specialty and the reason the shop outgrew Fleet Street and moved into a much larger waterfront space in 2024. It sells cookies, including in gift boxes, but a chocolate chip cookie is not the headline. Two hundred metres from Pitango, so checking both costs you nothing.

menu.name: Chocolate chip cookie

menu.name: Macaron
menu.note: The actual specialty.

menu.name: Éclair
menu.note: Second read on their pastry cream.

stops.name: Café Dear Leon
stops.blurb: The original, on O'Donnell Square, and it opens at 6am, earlier than anything else here. Strong pastry programme, and the s'mores cookie is the one that shows up in every photo. The coffee matters more than it sounds like it should when you are five cookies deep and need to reset your palate.

menu.name: Chocolate chip cookie
menu.note: Rotates through the pastry case.

menu.name: S'mores cookie
menu.note: The house signature.

menu.name: Cortado
menu.note: The palate reset that saves the tour.

stops.name: Ovenbird Bakery
stops.blurb: The third Ovenbird and the one with the longest hours, open until 7 on weekdays. If you are starting late, this is often the only serious bakery in the city still open. Same Chocolate ChiRp as the other two.

menu.name: Chocolate ChiRp Cookie
menu.note: Shaved Belgian milk chocolate, Maldon salt.

menu.name: Morning bun
menu.note: Gone by mid morning.

menu.name: Country sourdough loaf
menu.note: Take one home.

stops.name: Zoe's Just Dezzerts
stops.blurb: The only Federal Hill stop still standing after a rough couple of years for bakeries down here. Cakes, cupcakes, tarts and cookies, with allergy friendly options that go further than most. Afternoons only, from half twelve, and closed Monday and Tuesday, so it is an end of tour stop rather than a start.

menu.name: Chocolate chip cookie
menu.note: Ask what came out today.

menu.name: Cupcake
menu.note: The thing they are best known for.

menu.name: Fruit tart
menu.note: A break from chocolate.

closedSince.name: Maillard Patisserie
closedSince.note: Both the Hampden and Hamilton shops shut in early May 2026. The owner cited the workload of running a small business. Common Ground, a hundred metres up the same street, took its place on this list.

closedSince.name: Dulceology Bakery
closedSince.note: Closed its Federal Hill storefront after six years. Zoe's Just Dezzerts, three blocks north, took its place on this list.
